bullets.text: Built a generative AI assistant researchers could trust: it checks gene names against official databases and falls back to a local list of 19,213 genes if they go down (LangChain, AWS).

Built a tool-calling LLM agent (LangChain, AWS Bedrock, Claude Haiku 4.5) for a multi-omics cancer research platform, with three tools for gene alias resolution, scoring-methodology explanation and dataset provenance.
Found where the assistant went wrong with about 65 automated checks at three levels, fixed failures layer by layer, and reused the checks after changing AI provider (pytest).
Collaborated with the client's engineers to put the tool into everyday use and reviewed their code changes with the CTO; it is now in live use (TypeScript, OpenAI).
Built a production RAG and agentic retrieval system (LLM API, LangChain, LangGraph, ChromaDB) served through a FastAPI REST API in Docker on the client's own server.
Wrote about 65 automated tests across 8 files at three levels, and used them to check the assistant still behaved after switching AI providers (pytest, AWS Bedrock).
Deployed the agent as a Docker container on AWS Lambda (Lambda Web Adapter) with ECR image pipelines, IAM execution roles and least-privilege policies.
Proposed and prototyped an MCP-based agentic tool in Python (FastMCP, Ollama gpt-oss:20b, PostgreSQL, GitHub Actions CI), presented in a live stakeholder demo.

Contributed the MCP implementation to the client's production repository (TypeScript/Node.js MCP server, OpenAI query generation, Convex database), now in live day-to-day use; engagement received a 5-star commendation from senior leadership.

paragraphs: Your team is building the AI foundations the rest of engineering ships on. That is the kind of problem I have been working on. For my AstraZeneca-affiliated MSc dissertation I built an AI assistant that researchers could trust: it checks its answers against official databases, keeps working when those services go down, and is checked by about 65 automated tests. When the project switched AI providers, the same tests showed it still behaved, and I wrote up how often it got answers wrong so the team knew where it could be trusted.

At 180 Degrees Consulting I led the design in a five-person team that turned a startup's vague idea into a working AI prototype in three months, which the client's engineers then put into everyday use. The client's founder later called it "stable, production-ready" and said it arrived "ahead of schedule". At a hackathon I built a tool that answers in under 3 seconds for about £0.003 per question, and as a freelancer I built a private client an AI finance assistant that runs on his own server to keep costs down. Before my MSc, at Avasoft, I helped ship the first release of a money-management app for a company's 10,000+ employees.
Your ad's focus on agentic systems with tool use and context is a big part of why I am applying.
Could we spend 20 minutes on how the team evaluates new models and prompts in production?
